reply_text:
I’d hold the merge. I found four issues comparing `excerpt-helper` with `main`:

1. **[P1] Short text is truncated, and every result gets an ellipsis** — `src/excerpt.js:6–8`  
   There’s no check for text already within the limit. `excerpt('hello world', 20)` returns `'hello…'`, losing a whole word; `excerpt('hello', 20)` returns `'hello…'`; empty input returns `'…'`. This contradicts the README’s unchanged-short-text and ellipsis-only-on-removal guarantees.

2. **[P2] A word ending exactly at the limit is unnecessarily dropped** — `src/words.js:2–4`  
   `slice(0, limit)` excludes the space at index `limit`, so the helper backs up to the previous space. `excerpt('one two three', 7)` returns `'one…'` rather than `'one two…'`, even though `one two` fits. The existing words test explicitly expects this incorrect boundary behavior.

3. **[P2] Markdown stripping deletes literal content** — `src/plain.js:3`  
   Removing every `*`, `_`, `~`, and backtick also removes characters that aren’t formatting markers. For example, `snake_case and 2 * 3` becomes `snakecase and 2 3`, and ``Use `a_b` here`` becomes `Use ab here`. This changes the preview’s meaning rather than just removing formatting.

4. **[P1] The helpers aren’t connected to card rendering** — new helpers in `src/excerpt.js` / `src/plain.js`; existing `src/card.js:2`  
   `card()` still returns only `entry.body.trim()`. Nothing calls either helper, so merging this branch won’t actually produce the advertised plain-text excerpts under cards.

**Validation:** all four existing tests pass; I reproduced the cases above with direct calls. No files changed.
